correctness.rationale: Translate any distance-two pair of rotations so that one word is z. Equal Parikh vectors make its two mismatches a swap. If two shifts had different swap pairs, take a symbol e involved only in the first. For its indicator f, D=R_s f−f has a unique +1, while R_t f=f for the other nonzero shift. Commutation gives R_t D=D, impossible because a nonzero cyclic translation fixes no coordinate. This holds even when z is periodic. In 012,021,120 the successive pairs swap {1,2} and {0,1}; common insertions add identical columns and therefore preserve these two mismatch pairs, making a common orbit impossible at any insertion length. The same invariant gives every length at least three by common padding. Length zero, one and two are trivial within each Parikh class; the frozen two-word boundary is exactly the published theorem for arbitrary finite alphabets. No binary three-word conclusion is needed.
residual_risks: Frozen enumeration was read but not executed; it corroborates the rigidity statement only up to its length cutoffs. The argument for arbitrarily long insertions is analytic.

evidence: The two-word sufficiency theorem is alphabet-general but not family-size-general. Gabrić proves a stronger description for two inequivalent shifts at distance two: periodic equal-length blocks except for one block with a one-symbol defect.
Shallit gives possible conjugate distances; Makhynko concerns binary rotational-distance counts. Neither addresses the triple insertion problem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger single-word structural theorem covers the auxiliary lemma, but the insertion obstruction is not a special case of pair sufficiency or a classification/count of rotations.

evidence: For two shifts, replace each by its unsigned cyclic shift size in [1,⌊n/2⌋]. Equal sizes are identical or inverse shifts and give the same unordered swap by rotation. For different sizes, Lemma 14 applies: both are multiples of g, so each moves the single defect block to a different block position without changing its internal index. Their swaps use the same two letters at the defect. Thus the frozen rigidity lemma is fully implied.

The multiword result uses the additional observation that the original exchange pairs persist under every common insertion, and supplies a smallest aligned triple forcing two different pairs. That result is not supplied by the orbit-structure theorem or the equalizability papers.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the full structural overlap, not merely a topic match. The supported distinct result is the solution and minimal witness in the common-insertion setting, which requires choosing incompatible mismatch columns and using their preservation, not just specializing n,i,j in Gabrić's theorem.

evidence: Thongjarast–Pasiphol–Ruangwises uses the same-position common-insertion definition and leaves equal-Parikh sufficiency for k≥3 open in §7. Shinagawa–Nuida §6 asks the multiple-word question and singles out a binary three-word question; its 0-cyclic restriction is not unrestricted ternary equalization.
Gabrić studies two shifts of one already given word, not the simultaneous expansion of several words.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equalizability comparison matches the operation, alphabet and quantifier over the family size, distinguishing zero-only insertion, two-word sufficiency and arbitrary-block insertion for three words.

originality.rationale: Pass applies to the distinct equalizability finding: a minimum-size ternary obstruction to common-insertion equalization and its extension to all lengths. The rotation-rigidity lemma in isolation is not a new structural consequence: it follows from Gabrić's earlier Lemma 14. The work uses the exchange-pair invariant across unchanged mismatch columns to connect that structure to the separate open multiple-word insertion problem.
residual_risks: Capped Resultary searches and a focused primary query do not establish priority. An uninspected paper may already have used this orbit structure to produce a multiple-word counterexample. No novelty is attributed to exchange-pair rigidity alone.

value.rationale: This gives a sharp negative answer to a stated extension of the pair theorem: equal symbol counts cease to be sufficient already at family size three and ternary length three, no matter how large the permitted identical insertions are. The two aligned swaps give a usable structural obstruction beyond the single example. Novelty of the supporting orbit lemma is not needed for that contribution.
residual_risks: The invariant need not decide arbitrary families; the binary three-word question and a full multiword characterization remain outside the result.
